title: Customer threads shortlist + experiment notes — April 17 2025
summary: Working shortlist of recurring customer threads (Apr 2025) condensed into 5 priority asks plus lightweight experiment probes. Purpose: surface low-effort experiments that can reduce churn risk and inform product/eng prioritization. Doc is intentionally terse — raw voice snippets included for stitching into ticket descriptions.
customer_highlights: Large enterprise fintech: extremely sensitive to per-request cost volatility; wants predictable per-call unit cost and breakdown by model variant.
Mid-market SaaS (PLG): frustrated with dropdown complexity in model selection and unexpected fallback behavior during spikes.
Platform team at a retailer: needs VPC/private deployment visibility for KV cache metrics and how autoscaling impacts latency SLAs.
Startups/AI-native: ask for quick rollback and canary tooling when quality regression is observed after model/quantization rollouts.
Several customers asking for actionable tuning suggestions (batch size, quantization profile) based on their observed token and latency distributions.
prioritized_requests: Console: transparent per-token cost breakdown (model + quantization + infra) on request detail page — customers say this turns a 'billing mystery' into an actionable config change.
Routing UI: small policy editor to create 'latency-first' and 'cost-first' routing presets, with simple toggles for region and fallback model.
Model pin preview: allow customers to preview pinned model behavior on a sandbox subset (10% traffic) before committing to full pin — reduces fear of regressions.
KV/Prefix cache visibility: expose hit-rate and effective token savings per-route so platform teams can justify cache sizes and scaling policy.
Quick rollback: one-click rollback to previous model/variant that also captures trace context for postmortem analysis (linked to tracing/console).
experiment_probes: A/B (ui): show per-token cost breakdown on request detail for a sample of 50 orgs for 7 days; measure 1) support ticket decline on billing questions, 2) changes to batching configs.
Canary-run (ops): enable 'model pin preview' for 12 pilot customers with a short guide; track rollback usage and satisfaction via 2-question follow-up survey.
Synthetic-load probe: create a workload that reduces cache hit to 60% and observe p95 latency and token cost delta across two autoscaling policies (current vs conservative).
Suggestion nudges: in console, surface one recommended batch size/quantization pair per route based on last 24h token distribution; see adoption and resulting cost delta over 14 days.
Fallback transparency: add a small banner when a request used a fallback model variant (why + latency delta); instrument whether this reduces churn-related tickets.
open_questions: What privacy/enterprise constraints do we need for model pin previews in Dedicated/Private deployments? (legal + security checklist)
How accurate is our current per-token cost attribution model when multiple optimizations (quantization + batching + cache) overlap? Need engineering confirmation.
Signal: what threshold of customer-reported billing confusion should trigger making cost breakdowns default-visible vs opt-in?
Should console 'nudge' suggestions be experimental-only (opt-in) to avoid surprising enterprise customers?
Telemetry cost: how much extra ingestion/storage will per-request cache-hit + cost fields add? Ops estimate required.
next_steps: Product: refine scope for per-token cost breakdown MVP and produce a one-pager for Eng (due 2025-04-25).
Eng/Runtime: validate per-token attribution accuracy and provide a small rubric for what counts as model vs infra cost by 2025-04-30 (JIRA-3724 assigned).
Customer Success: recruit 12 pilot customers for model pin preview (reach out by 2025-04-24).
Design: quick UI mocks for routing presets + fallback banner (prototype link in linked_artifacts) — review 2025-04-28.
SRE: estimate telemetry/ingestion impact of adding cache metrics to per-request traces (deliver estimate 2025-04-29).
raw_snippets: 'We keep getting invoices that jump around — I just want to see what part of my token bill is from the new quantized model.' — Platform lead, fintech customer
'During peak loads our app silently falls back to a cheaper model and users notice lower quality. We need to be able to see and opt out of that fallback.' — Product manager, mid-market SaaS
'If you suggested a batch size that actually reduced our unit cost we'd probably enable it — but we're nervous about latency spikes.' — Engineering lead, AI startup
'Can you show us cache hit-rate history per route? We want to justify buying reserved capacity.' — Infra lead, retail customer
'Rollback needs to be quick and reversible to avoid finger-pointing in incidents.' — SRE, enterprise customer
